transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Grace, Marcus, thanks so much for making time today, I know Thursday afternoons are tough to carve out. How's everyone doing?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Doing well, thanks, just back from a plant visit in Ohio so glad to be sitting down for a bit.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Same here, good to finally connect, we've been meaning to look into this for a while.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Glad we could line it up. I've got Lena here with me, she's one of our solutions engineers and she'll help answer anything technical that comes up.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Hey both, nice to meet you, looking forward to hearing more about what you're dealing with over there.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Likewise.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: So before I show anything, I'd love to just understand your world a bit better. Marcus, can you walk me through how Acme handles analytics and reporting today?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Sure. Honestly it's a mess. We've got data spread across our ERP, a warehouse management system, and then a Tableau instance that maybe six people in the company actually know how to use.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: And most of operations, the plant managers, the regional ops leads, they're stuck waiting on Marcus's team to pull reports for them, which creates this huge bottleneck.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: How often are they asking for reports?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Constantly, probably twenty to thirty ad hoc requests a week across my team of three analysts. We're basically a human API at this point.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That's a really common pain point we hear, especially in manufacturing and logistics where the frontline managers need numbers fast but aren't going to write SQL.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Exactly, that's our world. We have twelve distribution centers and each regional lead wants to see their own throughput, on-time delivery, and inventory turns basically in real time, not three days later in a PDF.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Got it. And when you say real time, what's actually acceptable, is it truly live, or more like refreshed daily?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Honestly daily would already be a massive improvement over what we have now, which is more like weekly for some of these reports. If we could get to hourly for the critical operational metrics that would be fantastic.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That's very doable on our end, our standard sync cadence is every fifteen minutes for most source systems, and we can do near real time with event streaming for a few use cases if needed.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: That already sounds better than what we've got.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Let's talk a bit about who else is involved in a decision like this. Grace, is it just you and Marcus, or is there a broader group?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: It's really the two of us driving it day to day, but our CFO, Renata, has to sign off on anything over fifty thousand a year, and IT security will need to review before anything touches our data.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Yeah, IT security review is usually the longest part of any vendor process here, just a heads up.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That's helpful to know early. We're SOC 2 Type Two certified and can share the report under NDA whenever you need it, that usually speeds up the security review a lot.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Perfect, that'll help, our security team always asks for that first thing.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: I'll get that report sent over to you both today so you have it in hand before it's even requested.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Appreciated.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: On budget, you mentioned fifty thousand as a threshold for CFO approval, is that roughly the ballpark you're expecting to spend annually, or could it go higher?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: We had budgeted somewhere between fifty and eighty thousand for the year depending on scope, we're comparing a couple vendors so it really depends what's included.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: That's helpful context. Just so you know where we typically land, for a company your size with twelve locations, most customers end up in our Growth tier, which is around sixty two thousand a year for up to fifty seats, and that includes the integrations you'd need.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: How many source systems can that connect to?

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Unlimited connections on Growth actually, it's seat based pricing not connector based, so you could plug in your ERP, your WMS, and Salesforce if you use it, all under the same plan.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: That's actually simpler than I expected, our other vendor we're evaluating charges per connector which was getting complicated fast.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Yeah we hear that a lot, we deliberately moved away from that model a couple years back because it punishes exactly the kind of company you are, lots of systems, not a huge team.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Who else are we up against, are you allowed to say, or is that awkward?

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Ha, I won't ask who specifically, but broadly we compete against the bigger BI incumbents and a couple of newer point solutions. Where we tend to win is ease of setup for non-technical users and speed to first dashboard.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: That matters a lot to us honestly, our last BI rollout basically failed because it took six months to get anyone using it and by then everyone had lost interest.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That's such a common story. Our median time from kickoff to first live dashboard is under two weeks for a company your size, and we do hands-on onboarding, it's not just documentation and a support ticket.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Two weeks, that includes connecting our ERP and WMS?

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Yep, assuming we get access and credentials promptly, two weeks is realistic for the core connections and your first set of dashboards. Full rollout to all twelve DCs with custom views per region usually takes another two to four weeks after that.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Okay, that's a lot faster than I was expecting honestly.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Let's talk timeline on your end, when are you hoping to have a decision made, and when would you want to actually be live?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: We'd like to make a vendor decision by the end of Q4, so call it mid-December, and ideally be live with at least the core dashboards by end of January before our fiscal year planning cycle starts.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: That planning cycle is a big driver honestly, leadership wants better visibility into throughput and on time delivery before they set next year's targets.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Got it, that gives us a clear target. If we can get security review moving early and get a technical deep dive scheduled soon, January go live is very achievable on our side.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: I'd suggest we set up a technical session next week where I walk through the actual connectors for your ERP, what's it running on by the way?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: It's an older SAP instance, plus a custom built WMS that our own engineering team maintains.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Okay, SAP is one of our most mature connectors, no concerns there. The custom WMS we'd want to look at together, probably a database level connection or an API if you expose one, either works.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: We do have a REST API on the WMS actually, I can get you the docs.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Perfect, if you can send that over before our technical session that'll let me come prepared with a real integration plan instead of just theory.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: I'll send the API docs by tomorrow.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Great. Grace, would it help to see a couple of reference customers in a similar space, maybe another logistics or manufacturing company using Beacon at a similar scale?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Yes actually, that would carry a lot of weight with our leadership team, real proof it works for a company like us.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: I'll set that up, we have a great reference at Northstar Logistics who's a similar size, I'll ask if they're open to a quick call and get that scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: That would be great, thank you.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Of course. One more thing while I have you, is there a specific use case or dashboard that if we nailed it, would make this an easy yes internally?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Honestly, on time delivery by region, broken down by carrier. If leadership could see that daily without me pulling a report, that alone would probably justify the whole thing.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: That's a great one to lead with, we can absolutely build that as one of the first dashboards in the technical session so you're seeing exactly that view.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: That would be perfect, honestly if you show up to the technical session with that already mocked up we'll be sold.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Noted, we'll make sure that's front and center. Let's recap where we land. I'll send over the SOC 2 report and a formal proposal reflecting the Growth tier pricing we discussed, both by end of this week.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Sounds good.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Lena will set up the technical deep dive for next week, Marcus will send the WMS API docs beforehand, and I'll get the Northstar Logistics reference call scheduled.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Perfect, I'll get those docs over tomorrow morning.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: And Grace, once you have the proposal, do you want me to also loop in Renata directly, or would you rather present internally first?

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Let me take a first pass internally, then if there are questions on the finance side I'll bring you and Renata together.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: That works, just let me know when. Anything else either of you want to cover before we wrap?

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: No, I think this was really helpful, appreciate you walking through the pricing so directly.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Agreed, this was a good use of thirty minutes, looking forward to the technical session.

transcript.speaker: Sam Whitfield
transcript.text: Great, thank you both, I'll get that SOC 2 report and proposal over today, and Lena will follow up on scheduling. Talk soon.

transcript.speaker: Lena Ortiz
transcript.text: Thanks everyone, looking forward to digging into the WMS integration next week.

transcript.speaker: Grace Liu
transcript.text: Thanks Sam, thanks Lena, bye.

transcript.speaker: Marcus Webb
transcript.text: Thanks all, bye.

summary.overview: Sam and Lena ran a discovery call with Grace Liu and Marcus Webb from Acme Corp, a logistics and manufacturing company evaluating Beacon to replace fragmented, analyst-bottlenecked reporting across SAP, a custom WMS, and Tableau. Acme's operations leaders need near-real-time visibility into throughput, on-time delivery, and inventory turns across twelve distribution centers, and currently wait on a three-person analyst team for ad hoc reports. Budget is expected in the $50K-$80K range with CFO approval required above $50K, and Acme wants a vendor decision by mid-December with a January go-live ahead of fiscal year planning. The call ended with clear next steps: a SOC 2 report, a formal proposal, a technical deep dive on the SAP and WMS integrations, and a customer reference call.
bullet_points: 🏭 Acme runs 12 distribution centers, reporting split across SAP, a custom WMS, and Tableau
📉 Analyst team fielding 20-30 ad hoc report requests per week, described as a 'human API'
💰 Budget range $50K-$80K/year, CFO sign-off required above $50K
🔒 SOC 2 Type II report requested to speed up Acme's IT security review
💵 Growth tier (~$62K/year, up to 50 seats, unlimited connectors) proposed as fit
⏱️ Target: vendor decision by mid-December, go-live by end of January
🔌 Integration scope: mature SAP connector plus custom WMS via REST API
🎯 On-time-delivery-by-carrier dashboard flagged as the 'easy yes' use case
